native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: Gardening-introduced plants dominate the non-native flora of wetlands (~56%), coastal habitats (~54%) and forests (where the sparse non-native flora is 88–100% gardening-derived), are intermediate in scrublands, riparian zones and meadows (31–40%), and are least prevalent in croplands (~19%) and rock outcrops (0%); urban plots host the most gardening species in absolute terms and the second-highest per-plot frequency but only a ~30% share because unintentional introductions also accumulate there. This habitat gradient parallels the regional rise of gardening as an introduction pathway (17% of pre-1500 introductions vs 75% in 1985–2019).
native_result.WorkflowB: Parsed tab-separated invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plots), validated pathway-count consistency, computed three prevalence metrics per habitat (pooled occurrence share, mean per-plot share, incidence), ran the zero-total-plot sensitivity check (occurrence-share ranking unchanged; incidence ranking shifted, both reported), one supportive chi-square on the pooled pathway×habitat table, and one sentence of temporal context from temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv; phylogeny excluded per instruction.

sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants introduced through gardening in the ten most widespread habitat types in Barcelona province.
sub_hypo.relations: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats; no direction of difference is specified.

sub_hypo.text: Gardening-introduced plants dominate non-native flora in wetlands, coastal habitats and forests, are intermediate in scrublands, riparian zones and meadows, and are least prevalent in croplands and rock outcrops.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants across 632 sampled plots in Barcelona province; habitat prevalence assessed using pooled occurrence share, mean per-plot share and incidence. Excluding zero-total plots leaves the occurrence-share ranking unchanged but changes the incidence ranking.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening-derived shares vary by habitat: approximately 56% in wetlands, 54% in coastal habitats, 88–100% in forests with sparse non-native flora, 31–40% in scrublands, riparian zones and meadows, 19% in croplands and 0% in rock outcrops. Pathway–habitat association was assessed with a chi-square test on pooled counts.

sub_hypo.text: Urban plots host the most gardening-introduced species in absolute terms and the second-highest per-plot frequency, but gardening accounts for only approximately 30% of non-native flora because unintentional introductions also accumulate there.
sub_hypo.context: Urban habitats compared with other habitats among 632 sampled plots in Barcelona province.
sub_hypo.relations: Urban plots rank highest in absolute gardening-species counts and second-highest in per-plot frequency, while their gardening-derived share is approximately 30%, alongside accumulated unintentional introductions.

sub_hypo.text: The habitat gradient in gardening-derived non-native flora parallels the regional rise of gardening as an introduction pathway, from 17% of introductions before 1500 to 75% in 1985–2019.
sub_hypo.context: Temporal introduction trends for non-native plants in Catalonia, used as supporting context for the habitat pattern in Barcelona province.
sub_hypo.relations: The gardening share of introductions increases from 17% before 1500 to 75% in 1985–2019; this temporal increase is described as paralleling the habitat gradient.

This habitat gradient parallels the regional rise of gardening as an introduction pathway (17% of pre-1500 introductions vs 75% in 1985–2019).
